now: The page now covers only the main scenario, N6, and the same scenario with a fixed first response. Earlier versions are kept in the repo.

steps.name: N6: main scenario, model writes its own first reply
N6f: same scenario, fixed first response
N6Rf: fixed first response across 4 wordings and 6 name sets

findings: N6, own first reply: helped 3/24, bystander 0/5, rescued 0/24, none 0/24. Bystander is small because the model often gives in its own first reply, which the scripted history ignores.
N6f, fixed first response: helped 4/24, controls 0/72.
N6Rf, fixed first response across wordings: helped 52, bystander 19, rescued 2, none 54, of 192 each.

Counting only gives that state the cost with a valid motive, of 48 per cell (helped/bystander/rescued/none): P0 10/1/0/2, P1 12/0/2/8, P2 7/0/0/1, P3 13/10/0/28. Helped beats pooled controls in P0 to P2 (p from 7e-5 to .003) but not in P3 (p=1). P-values are approximate and motive labels are one rater's.
Only 27 of 52 helped gives are labelled reciprocity. Group reasons account for 87 of all 127 gives, and 61 gives imply a false gain in survivors.
P3's no-one-benefits line never mentions who survives. That is the likely cause of its different results, but it has not been tested.
decisions: Greedy decoding, thinking off, bf16, no blessings.
Recommended next: test the P3 cause by swapping in P0's sentence.
